citation: Brimicombe et al. (2022). Thermofeel: A python thermal comfort indices library. SoftwareX 18, 101005. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.softx.2022.101005
description: thermofeel is an ECMWF Python library for deriving human thermal-comfort and heat or cold stress indices from environmental variables. It calculates UTCI, several heat indices, wet-bulb globe temperature, PMV/PPD and related quantities, including radiant temperature and humidity. Inputs are meteorological conditions required by the chosen index; outputs are calculated indices or intermediate physical quantities. Coverage is global and inherited from user-supplied weather data, with no fixed map resolution or observation period. Public source and pip installation are free under Apache-2.0. A limitation is that optional radiation approximations estimate missing variables and should not be confused with measured radiation. Version 2 also changes the API, so workflows written for version 1 require updates. The library can translate climate or building-simulation conditions into heat-exposure indicators for infrastructure planning, complementary to EnergyPlus (model-energyplus). The README documents functions, migration issues and the 2022 SoftwareX paper. No weather grids were retrieved, and index values were not independently recalculated.
